title: The Waggle Dance
topic: วิทยาศาสตร์
lines: Honeybees cannot talk, but they have a clever way of sharing information.
When a worker bee finds a good source of flowers, she flies back to the
hive and performs a special movement called the "waggle dance." **It**
tells the other bees exactly where the flowers are.
During the dance, the bee walks in a straight line while shaking her body,
then circles back and repeats the movement. The direction of the straight
line shows the direction of the flowers compared with the sun, and the
length of time **she** shakes shows how far away they are. A longer waggle
means a longer flight. **Those** watching the dance can then fly directly
to the food, sometimes several kilometers away.
The scientist who first explained this behavior, Karl von Frisch, won a
Nobel Prize in 1973. At first, **many** did not believe that insects could
communicate so precisely. Today, researchers use **his** findings to help
protect bee populations, which are falling in many parts of the world.
